_README: Copy this file to <site-root>/tools/deny-list.json and fill it in, or pass
--deny-list <file> / set $ORACLE_DENY_LIST. It ships EMPTY on purpose: a
deny-list is the one artifact that would carry the names it exists to keep
out of the build, so it belongs beside the site, never inside a shared plugin.
check-grammar.js warns on every run until customerNames is non-empty.
_customerNames: Every customer, partner and end-client name the catalog must never print,
in every spelling anyone has used: the legal name, the trading name, the
misspelling in the source deck, the group abbreviation. Matched as whole
words against the raw text of content.js and review.js, so a name that is
also an ordinary word needs no escaping but will match that word too.
_bannedStrings: Site-specific substrings that must never reach content.js, each with the
reason printed on failure. Use it for: internal company or product names,
internal deal-state vocabulary, figures out of a confidential business case,
third-party products named inside a customer's estate, personal mailboxes,
and any phrase an owner has retired in a review round. Matched as plain
Example shape: [["\u20ac190K", "customer economics from a confidential case"]]
